## (1) Cause, and the evidence that qualifies your hypothesis

**The mechanism is exactly where you point, and it is owner-local.**

- The printer already implements upstream's anchor: `printer.rs:8452-8459` maps the close brace at `statement_list_end`, and `printer.rs:8136-8142` defines that as `array.end`, **gated on `array.end != u32::MAX`** — the synthetic sentinel. So "no range on the statements array" ⇒ silently no close-brace mapping, no other path involved.
- `system.rs:4369 create_block` always goes through `factory.create_node_array` → `alloc_synthetic_array` (factory.rs:5459/5492), which never sets pos/end. Every System block, including the execute body at line 811, therefore reaches the printer with the sentinel.
- Upstream keeps the array: `createBlock(executeStatements, true)` (_tsc.js:117044) where `executeStatements = visitNodes2(node.statements, topLevelVisitor, isStatement, statementOffset)`, and `createNodeArray` returns an existing NodeArray unchanged.

**Correction to the hypothesis: upstream's preservation is conditional, and the range is not the parse tree's.** `visitNodes2` (_tsc.js:91087-91115):

```js
if (start > 0 || count < length2) { hasTrailingComma = …; }   // pos/end stay -1
else { pos = nodes.pos; end = nodes.end; … }
…
setTextRangePosEnd(updatedArray, pos, end);
```

So the execute array keeps a range **iff `statementOffset == 0`**, and the range it keeps is that of `node.statements` **as the System transform receives it** — i.e. whatever earlier transforms left behind, not necessarily the parse-tree array. Rust drops it unconditionally, so the divergence appears only in the `offset == 0` subset. That also explains why only the close brace differs and the open brace does not: the Block *node* stays synthesized in both implementations (`emitTokenWithComment(OpenBraceToken, node.pos …)` with `pos = -1`), and only the array carries a position. Your observation that the open brace matches is corroboration, not a coincidence.

**Evidence in-repo that contradicts a blanket "offset == 0 ⇒ attach the parse range" fix.** `ratchets/h2-6c-qualification.v1.json` contains the only frozen System + `sourceMap:true` rows: `typescript-6.0.3/compiler/outModuleConcatSystem.ts#target%3Des5` and `#target%3Des2015` (also `declaration`, `outFile`). Decoding the frozen upstream `all.js.map` against `all.js`, the mapped output lines are 23-27 and 43-49 only: **the `execute` close braces (the `        }` lines) carry no mapping**, even though neither source file has a prologue directive, so `statementOffset == 0` there too. Under a blanket fix those two gated rows would gain a segment and regress.

The consistent reading of both facts is that by the time System runs, the incoming statements array in the bundle case has already lost its range (class lowering rebuilding the statement list), while in your `export {}; const = 5;` case at ES5 it has not. That is also upstream's behaviour: System forwards, it does not re-derive.

**Why the old80 passed**: not because System is generally right, but because none of them hit `offset == 0` *with* a surviving incoming range. Note that the in-repo System coverage (`ratchets/h2-1d-qualification.v1.json`, 6 cases) sets no `sourceMap` at all, so this anchor was never exercised by the frozen ladder. I would not treat "old80 green" as evidence about the rule until you check the two conditions on those inputs.

I see nothing implicating the empty variable list itself; see the discriminator control below.

## (2) Smallest owner-local correction

In `system.rs::transform_source_file` only, at the execute body (line 811), after `create_block(execute, true)`:

- if `offset == 0` **and** the incoming array's `pos`/`end` are not the sentinel, copy them onto the execute block's statements array;
- otherwise leave the sentinel (today's behaviour).

The range source must be the **incoming** `original_array` record (the SourceFile statements array as System received it), not the parse-tree array — that is what makes the two 6c bundle rows stay unmapped without a special case.

No new API is needed: `factory.rs:5533 set_node_array_text_range` already exists with exactly `setTextRange(nodeArray, …)` semantics and is already used by the es2015 class-body lanes. Do **not** touch `create_block` — its other 8 call sites, including the outer `System.register` body at line 845, correspond to upstream `createBlock(plainArray)` and must stay unranged. No printer change, no relaxation of the `u32::MAX` gate (a "fall back to the node end" would invent mappings globally), no parser/comment-metadata change.

**Second boundary you must plan for:** `statement_list_end` also feeds `emit_comments_before_close_brace` (printer.rs:8441-8447), and the array is also the fallback input to `detached_comment_prefix_for_node_array` when `relocated_statement_list_comments` is absent (printer.rs:8168-8180). Giving the execute array a real range therefore changes comment lookup for that block, in the same direction upstream does. That is the reason the comment controls below are not optional.

## (3) Controls that constrain the fix

1. **The two frozen 6c rows** `outModuleConcatSystem.ts#target%3Des5` / `#target%3Des2015` must stay byte-identical (js, map, d.ts). They are already in the gated corpus and are the counterexample that a blanket fix breaks.
2. **Non-recovery discriminator** — the cheapest falsification: `export {};\nconst x = 5;\n`, System, ES5 and ES2015, `sourceMap` on. My prediction is that it reproduces your mismatch with no recovery input at all. If it does **not** reproduce, the diagnosis is wrong and the empty-declaration list is implicated, not System.
3. **`statementOffset > 0` twin**: `"use strict";\nexport {};\nconst x = 5;\n` — must remain *unmapped* after the fix. This proves the port is conditional rather than blanket; a blanket implementation passes (2) and fails here.
4. **Custom-prologue twin** (the second contributor to `offset`, since your loop advances past custom prologues too) — e.g. an `importHelpers` input that puts a helper import ahead of the execute body: also unmapped.
5. **Comment matrix on the execute close brace**: trailing comment immediately before `}` of the execute body, and a detached leading comment, each with `removeComments` false/true — the range now feeds the comment path.
6. **Execute-body shape variants** that change construction: top-level `await` (async execute modifiers), `export *` prelude, and an empty execute body (no statements ⇒ upstream still has an array with a range; confirm the empty case).
7. Keep the declaration and declaration-map writes in the assertion tuple, since they are currently equal and must stay so.

**Boundary / mutual review.** If control 1 regresses after the System-local change, the owner is not System: it is whichever earlier transform preserves or drops the SourceFile statements array range (the class-lowering/lexical-environment merge lane). Correcting *that* changes the close-brace anchor for every block in every transform, which is well outside this fix — I would want a joint review of the array-range policy before any such edit rather than special-casing System to compensate.

I have not run TypeScript or minted anything; items 1 and the upstream rule come from `ratchets/h2-6c-qualification.v1.json` and `vendor/typescript-6.0.3/lib/_tsc.js` as committed. Nothing here is a completion claim for the in-flight 96 commands, and I make no claim about the other tuple fields of the failing cases.
